activities.title: New Material: Parameter, Memory, and Compute Arithmetic

source_resources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
source_resources.author: Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, Tom Henighan, Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Chess, Rewon Child, Scott Gray, Alec Radford, Jeffrey Wu, Dario Amodei
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Basic calculus, logarithms, and parameter counting fundamentals.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational empirical study formulating power laws governing cross-entropy loss with respect to model parameters N, dataset size D, and compute C.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Scaling formulas, power-law exponents, and parameter compute trade-offs are derived in the lesson text.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Rosenfeld et al. A Constructive Prediction of the Generalization Error of Neural Networks
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Early formulation of power-law scaling; Kaplan focuses explicitly on autoregressive transformer language models.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Hestness et al. Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: General vision/translation scaling; Kaplan specifically establishes modern decoder-only LLM compute budgeting.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 2.1 Parameter and Compute Scaling of Transformers (C ≈ 6N FLOPs per token)

source_resources.title: Transformer Math 101
source_resources.author: Quentin Anthony, Stella Biderman, Hailey Schoelkopf
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under Creative Commons Attribution license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Transformer matrix dimensions and matrix multiplication FLOP counting.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Widely cited, practical industry guide deriving 6ND compute FLOPs, activation memory, KV cache size, and VRAM estimation.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The 6ND derivation (2ND forward, 4ND backward) and peak VRAM estimation models are fully worked out in the curriculum.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Narayanan et al. Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Rigorous academic formulation; Transformer Math 101 provides accessible step-by-step arithmetic equations.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Kaplan et al. Section 2.1 Compute Budgeting
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original 6ND approximation; EleutherAI expands on activation memory and KV cache.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Compute Requirements (C = 6PD) and Memory Requirements: Training

source_resources.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
source_resources.author: Samyam Rajbhandari, Jeff Rasley, Olatunji Ruwase, Yuxiong He
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Adam optimizer mechanics from Day 34 and parameter memory arithmetic.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Source of the 16 bytes per parameter accounting for mixed-precision Adam that the lesson's memory arithmetic uses.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete analytical formulas for bytes-per-parameter across AdamW vs SGD and mixed precision are fully provided.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Shoeybi et al. Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Focuses on tensor slicing and inter-GPU communication; ZeRO provides the standard breakdown of optimizer and parameter memory footprints.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Micikevicius et al. Mixed Precision Training
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Foundational mixed-precision paper; ZeRO formalizes the exact 16-byte Adam state footprint.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 3.1 Model States: Optimizer States, Gradients and Parameters (2Ψ + 2Ψ + KΨ = 16Ψ bytes, K = 12)

source_resources.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
source_resources.author: Ilya Loshchilov, Frank Hutter
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation and reference under arXiv open access terms; no paper figures or prose reproduced.
source_resources.prerequisites: Stochastic gradient descent, L2 regularization, and momentum concepts from Days 31-33.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational primary literature defining AdamW, demonstrating that L2 regularization does not equal decoupled weight decay in adaptive gradient algorithms.
source_resources.safe_fallback: All update equations and mathematical proofs are self-contained in the curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Kingma & Ba: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization (2014)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original Adam algorithm implementing L2 regularization via gradient addition, leading to sub-optimal generalization compared to decoupled weight decay.
Standard library reference; Loshchilov & Hutter provides theoretical mathematical derivations and empirical justification.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-Based Update (Algorithm 2, AdamW)

source_resources.title: nanoGPT: train.py pretraining loop
source_resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under MIT open source license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch, and Day 46-48 Transformer model architecture.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Compact historical code reference for the named implementation functions; CS336 spring2025 provides the lead component exercises. Do not infer top-p, atomic persistence or cloud budget enforcement from nanoGPT.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Runnable pretraining scripts and step-by-step tensor mechanics are fully self-contained in the curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Heavy abstraction layer wrapping distributed training; nanoGPT exposes raw PyTorch loops without framework overhead.
High-performance enterprise distributed framework; unsuitable for local educational first-principles comprehension.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: train.py: optimizer = model.configure_optimizers(weight_decay, learning_rate, (beta1, beta2), device_type); train.py: get_lr(it): linear warmup over warmup_iters, cosine decay to min_lr by lr_decay_iters; clip_grad_norm_(grad_clip) in the training loop
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Historical implementation reference: nanoGPT README marks the repository deprecated (November 2025). Toy CPU reading/runs do not establish full GPU pretraining feasibility.

source_resources.selection_rationale: Compact historical code reference for the named implementation functions; CS336 spring2025 provides the lead component exercises. Do not infer top-p, atomic persistence or cloud budget enforcement from nanoGPT.

Includes advanced production features (RoPE, GQA), but nanoGPT's simplicity is ideal for the core Days 46-48 assembly.

source_resources.title: The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
source_resources.author: Ari Holtzman, Jan Buys, Li Du, Maxwell Forbes, Yejin Choi
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Softmax probabilities, cumulative probability distributions from Days 25-27 and 41-42.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary source introducing Nucleus (Top-p) sampling and analyzing the failure of greedy decoding (loops, repetition).
source_resources.safe_fallback: Top-p truncation algorithms and worked probability cutoffs are completely explained in the lesson.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Fan et al. Hierarchical Neural Story Generation (Top-k)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Introduces top-k sampling; Holtzman et al. dynamic nucleus threshold is compared directly against top-k.
Practical library guide; Holtzman provides the foundational mathematical reasoning.

source_resources.title: PyTorch Tutorial: Saving and Loading Models
source_resources.author: PyTorch Documentation Team
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under BSD open source documentation license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch tensors and nn.Module basics.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Official documentation detailing state_dict serialization, optimizer state saving, and safe loading patterns.
